minor.issue: Pre-existing from iter5 — lockout uses request.client.host which is the K8s ingress proxy pod IP, not the real client IP. Works on localhost (5x 401 → 429) but is bypassable through the public URL. Fix: derive ip from request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or request.client.host fallback in core.check_login_lockout caller.

issues: Google Maps placeholder key causes Google's gray 'Oops! Something went wrong' overlay inside tracking-map. EXPECTED per problem statement (REACT_APP_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY_HERE). Sidebar (status, cost, origin/destination, driver, currency switch, share) renders correctly. Consider replacing this with a friendlier branded placeholder image when key is missing — non-blocking.

(LOW UX) PublicTracking currency switch keeps the previous EUR/MAD selection across queries — confirmed working; just document in i18n that 'price' returned by /api/public/orders/{id}/tracking is in `currency` field's native unit (the order's stored currency) and the UI does the conversion using a constant EXCHANGE_RATE_MAD_EUR=0.092. Hard-coded rate may drift; consider fetching from an FX endpoint or surfacing it as a config.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/orders.py public_order_tracking: uses projection {'_id': 0} on both orders.find_one and users.find_one — good. Live WS location correctly overrides DB current_location when present. Origin/destination only populated when origin_lat AND destination_lat are non-null, so normal (non-express) orders return origin=destination=null (acceptable since map is express-focused).

PublicTracking.js DEMO_ORDERS is hard-coded inside the bundle for ORD-4821 / ORD-4823 — fine for demo, but the price stored there is MAD (e.g. 850, 180) and the formatCurrency function treats `amount` as MAD then multiplies by 0.092 to get EUR. For REAL orders returned by /api/public/orders/{id}/tracking the price is whatever the customer chose (EUR in our test → 99) but the same formatCurrency assumes MAD as the base — i.e. switching to MAD on a real EUR-priced order shows '1.076,09 MAD' (99 / 0.092 ≈ 1076), which works because the EXCHANGE constant happens to be reciprocal-consistent, but if the real order currency is already EUR the MAD display is a back-conversion. Consider normalising: convert to MAD-base on load (e.g. const priceMAD = currency==='EUR' ? price/RATE : price) so the unit semantics are explicit.
PublicTracking.js useEffect doing axios.get(`${API}/public/orders/${id}/tracking`) does NOT send the Authorization header — verified. No CORS issue observed.

RiderApp.js html5-qrcode lifecycle: startScan/stopScan refactor cleanly toggles rider-scanner overlay; when camera unavailable a Spanish error is shown (good UX). Verified the overlay closes via rider-scan-cancel.
CustomerDashboard public-track-btn: anchor with data-testid present in express banner — navigation to /track works. Tap target adequate.

Backend GET /api/public/orders/{order_id}/tracking returns updated_at as an ISO string (it was stored as ISO string by create_express_order); the contract returns it unchanged — acceptable since the frontend renders it via new Date().toLocaleString().

rca of the issue: No new bug found in BLOQUE B / rider QR. Carry-over: brute-force lockout bypassable through K8s ingress (see iter5 RCA — identifier built from request.client.host = proxy pod IP). Map 'Oops' overlay is expected behavior of the @react-google-maps/api loader when given a placeholder key (InvalidKeyMapError) — the page-level MapErrorBoundary catches downstream render errors but Google's own JS API draws the gray overlay inside the GoogleMap container before any React error is thrown, which is why MapErrorBoundary's fallback is not shown. If a friendlier placeholder is desired, check `loadError` from useJsApiLoader and short-circuit-render the custom fallback BEFORE rendering <GoogleMap />.
